title: 计算机科学，从零搭建 · 第61部分：做研究

chapters.Outro: 回顾、习题，以及它们会在哪里再出现

aadf3bae3da6.en: Here is one C program, compiled once, timed on this machine. <bookmark mark='a'/> The only thing we change between runs is the size of an environment variable the program never reads, from nothing to four kilobytes. <bookmark mark='b'/> The median time moves by up to 7 percent. In 2009 Todd Mytkowicz and colleagues showed that such changes shift where the stack begins, and with it the alignment of hot data, and that this alone could decide which of two compiler settings looked faster. <bookmark mark='c'/> But is our spread that effect, or only noise? This machine randomizes where the stack begins on every run, which smears the effect out, and chapter two will show that noise alone could explain what we see. Telling the two apart, and not fooling yourself, is what this part is about.
aadf3bae3da6.zh: 这是一个 C 程序，只编译一次，在这台机器上计时。<bookmark mark='a'/>每次运行之间，我们唯一改变的，是一个程序从来不读的环境变量的大小，从空的到4千字节。<bookmark mark='b'/>中位时间的变动最多达到百分之7。2009年，Todd Mytkowicz 和同事们表明，这样的改变会移动栈的起始位置，连带改变热点数据的对齐，而单是这一点，就可能决定两种编译器设置里哪一种看起来更快。<bookmark mark='c'/>但我们看到的这个波动，是那种效应，还是只是噪声？这台机器每次运行都会随机化栈的起始位置，这会把效应抹平；第二章会表明，单凭噪声就足以解释我们看到的东西。把这两者区分开，并且不骗自己，就是这一部分要讲的。

6d3c8391b682.en: This series has quoted perhaps a thousand results. Where do they come from? <bookmark mark='a'/> Every one began as a question sharp enough that an answer could be wrong. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then a method: a proof, a measurement, or something built. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then evidence good enough to convince a sceptic who wants you to be wrong. <bookmark mark='d'/> And a paper, written so that others can check it. This last part is about doing that yourself.
6d3c8391b682.zh: 这个系列大概引用了上千个结果。它们是从哪里来的？<bookmark mark='a'/>每一个都始于一个问题，它尖锐到答案有可能是错的。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后是一种方法：一个证明、一次测量，或者造出来的某个东西。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后是证据，好到足以说服一个巴不得你出错的怀疑者。<bookmark mark='d'/>最后是一篇论文，写出来让别人能够检验。最后这一部分，讲的就是你自己怎样做到这些。

411c3ec97b25.en: This is Part 61 of Computer Science, Built, the last part of the series. <bookmark mark='a'/> We will reproduce measurement bias; time things rigorously, with intervals and repetitions; see how benchmarks fail; use proof and computer search to settle conjectures, or at least their small cases; learn to read, review, find problems and write; and gather the open problems the series met onto one map.
411c3ec97b25.zh: 这是《计算机科学，从零搭建》的第61部分，也是这个系列的最后一部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>我们会重现测量偏差；用区间和重复，严谨地给事情计时；看看基准测试是怎样失效的；用证明和计算机搜索来解决猜想，或者至少解决它们的小情形；学习阅读、评审、寻找问题和写作；最后把这个系列遇到过的开放问题汇集到一张地图上。

c3f1b1ee81a4.en: Research begins with a question, but not just any question. <bookmark mark='a'/> Does the environment affect speed? As asked, no experiment could ever say no. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sharpen it: which variable, which program, which machine, and compared with what. Now the answer could come out either way, and that is what makes it worth asking. <bookmark mark='c'/> A sharp question becomes a hypothesis; the hypothesis makes a prediction; and a test checks the prediction. <bookmark mark='d'/> If the test could have refuted it and did not, the hypothesis survives, for now. If it is refuted, you have learned something, and you come back with a better one. In 1934 the philosopher Karl Popper made this the mark of a scientific claim: that some observation could prove it wrong. A question whose answer you already know is not research, and neither is a claim that no result could ever contradict.
c3f1b1ee81a4.zh: 研究始于一个问题，但不是随便什么问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>环境会影响速度吗？照这样问，没有任何实验能回答说不。<bookmark mark='b'/>把它磨尖：哪个变量，哪个程序，哪台机器，和什么相比。现在答案两种都有可能，正是这一点让它值得一问。<bookmark mark='c'/>一个尖锐的问题变成一个假设；假设给出一个预测；而一次检验去核对这个预测。<bookmark mark='d'/>如果检验本可以驳倒它，却没有驳倒，这个假设就存活下来，暂时如此。如果它被驳倒了，你就学到了东西，然后带着一个更好的假设回来。1934年，哲学家 Karl Popper 把这一点当作科学主张的标志：某个观察有可能证明它是错的。一个你已经知道答案的问题不是研究，一个任何结果都无法反驳的主张也不是。

cbb283e4d6c6.en: Computer science answers questions with three kinds of evidence. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first is proof: a chain of steps from accepted axioms, like Turing's proof in 1936 that no program decides halting, from Part 25. A reader checks every step, or, since Part 54, a proof assistant does. <bookmark mark='b'/> The second is experiment: a controlled comparison, repeated, like the measurement-bias study at the heart of this part. It is checked when someone else runs it again and gets the same answer. <bookmark mark='c'/> The third is construction: build the thing and show that it works, like Dennis Ritchie and Ken Thompson's 1974 paper on Unix, the system behind Part 31. It is checked when others use it and it holds up. <bookmark mark='d'/> Most papers mix the three: a system built, measured, and a theorem about why it works. What a paper claims decides which evidence it owes.
cbb283e4d6c6.zh: 计算机科学用三种证据来回答问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一种是证明：从公认的公理出发的一串步骤，比如第25部分里图灵1936年的证明：没有任何程序能判定停机。读者检查每一步，或者，从第54部分起，由证明助手来检查。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二种是实验：一次受控的、重复进行的比较，比如这一部分核心的测量偏差研究。当别人再做一遍并得到同样的答案时，它就得到了检验。<bookmark mark='c'/>第三种是构造：把东西造出来，并表明它能工作，比如 Dennis Ritchie 和 Ken Thompson 1974年关于 Unix 的论文，Unix 就是第31部分背后的系统。当别人使用它、而它经得住考验时，它就得到了检验。<bookmark mark='d'/>大多数论文把这三种混在一起：造一个系统，测量它，再加一条关于它为什么能工作的定理。一篇论文主张什么，决定了它欠读者哪种证据。

214a8e52feb6.en: Results travel as papers, and papers have a shape. <bookmark mark='a'/> A title and authors; an abstract; an introduction; background; the idea or design; the evaluation, or the proofs; related work; a conclusion; and references. The order varies by field, but the parts recur. <bookmark mark='b'/> The abstract tells the whole story in about four sentences: the context, the problem, what we did, and what we found. <bookmark mark='c'/> Each remaining part answers one of the three questions every reader, and every reviewer, asks. Does it matter? That is the introduction's job: the problem, why it matters, and a list of contributions. <bookmark mark='d'/> Is it right? That is the evaluation or the proofs, with their limits stated. <bookmark mark='e'/> Is it new? That is related work: what was already known, and exactly what this paper adds. Chapter six reads papers with these questions in mind.
214a8e52feb6.zh: 结果以论文的形式传播，而论文有固定的形状。<bookmark mark='a'/>标题和作者；摘要；引言；背景；想法或设计；评估，或者证明；相关工作；结论；以及参考文献。顺序因领域而异，但这些部分反复出现。<bookmark mark='b'/>摘要用大约四句话讲完整个故事：背景、问题、我们做了什么，以及我们发现了什么。<bookmark mark='c'/>其余每一部分，回答每个读者、也是每个审稿人都会问的三个问题之一。它重要吗？这是引言的任务：问题是什么，为什么重要，再加一份贡献清单。<bookmark mark='d'/>它对吗？这是评估或证明的任务，并且要说明它们的局限。<bookmark mark='e'/>它新吗？这是相关工作的任务：已经知道了什么，以及这篇论文究竟增加了什么。第六章会带着这些问题去读论文。

712b66a6c0ed.en: Where do papers go? In most sciences, to journals. Computer science is unusual. <bookmark mark='a'/> Its main venues are selective conferences. A paper meets a fixed deadline, is read by three or more members of a programme committee, the authors may answer in a short rebuttal, and within a few months it is accepted or rejected, then presented in a talk and printed in the proceedings. <bookmark mark='b'/> Many have long histories: the Symposium on Operating Systems Principles since 1967, the theory symposium STOC since 1969, and the programming-languages symposium POPL since 1973; many accept fewer than one paper in four. <bookmark mark='c'/> Journals work differently: submit any time, and go through rounds of review and revision that can take months or years. In computer science they often hold the longer, fuller version of a conference paper, and preprints appear on arXiv first. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2009 Lance Fortnow argued that the field should grow up and move back toward journals. The debate continues.
712b66a6c0ed.zh: 论文发到哪里？在大多数科学里，发到期刊。计算机科学与众不同。<bookmark mark='a'/>它的主要发表场所是严格筛选的会议。一篇论文要赶一个固定的截止日期，由程序委员会的三名或更多成员审读，作者可以写一份简短的答辩（rebuttal），几个月之内论文就被接收或拒绝，然后在报告中宣讲，并印进会议论文集。<bookmark mark='b'/>许多会议历史悠久：操作系统原理研讨会始于1967年，理论研讨会 STOC 始于1969年，程序设计语言研讨会 POPL 始于1973年；许多会议的接收率不到四分之一。<bookmark mark='c'/>期刊的运作方式不同：随时可以投稿，然后经过一轮又一轮的审稿和修改，可能要花几个月甚至几年。在计算机科学里，期刊上登的常常是会议论文更长、更完整的版本，而预印本会先出现在 arXiv 上。<bookmark mark='d'/>2009年，Lance Fortnow 主张，这个领域应该长大，重新转向期刊。争论仍在继续。

d609bc633825.en: Here is this part's own experiment, written as a paper would be. <bookmark mark='a'/> The question: does an unused environment variable, or the order of linking, change the time of one C program on this machine? <bookmark mark='b'/> The method: thirty-three sizes, five runs each, interleaved; three link orders, fifteen runs each; medians compared with the run-to-run noise. <bookmark mark='c'/> The evidence: the medians spread by about seven percent across sizes and under one percent across link orders, both within the noise. <bookmark mark='d'/> Threats to validity, the section honest papers never skip: a shared machine, one program, one compiler, and address randomization switched on. <bookmark mark='e'/> The conclusion: no effect shown here, which is not the same as no effect. The next chapter takes that experiment apart.
d609bc633825.zh: 这是这一部分自己的实验，按一篇论文的写法写出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>问题：一个没用到的环境变量，或者链接的顺序，会不会改变这台机器上一个 C 程序的运行时间？<bookmark mark='b'/>方法：33种大小，每种运行五次，交错进行；三种链接顺序，每种运行15次；把中位数和每次运行之间的噪声相比较。<bookmark mark='c'/>证据：在各种大小之间，中位数相差大约百分之七；在各种链接顺序之间，相差不到百分之一，两者都在噪声范围之内。<bookmark mark='d'/>效度威胁，这是诚实的论文从不跳过的一节：一台共享的机器，一个程序，一个编译器，并且地址随机化是开着的。<bookmark mark='e'/>结论：这里没有显示出效应，而这和没有效应不是一回事。下一章会把这个实验拆开来看。

b8bc379c166f.en: Why would a variable nobody reads matter? <bookmark mark='a'/> When Linux starts a program, it copies the environment strings and the arguments to the very top of the new stack, then the pointers to them, and only below those do the program's own frames begin. <bookmark mark='b'/> So every byte added to the environment pushes every frame down. Write the address of a hot local variable as the top, minus the environment, minus everything else. <bookmark mark='c'/> The calling convention keeps the stack aligned to sixteen bytes, so the address moves in sixteen-byte steps. <bookmark mark='d'/> Within a sixty-four-byte cache line, from Part 9, it can sit in four places, <bookmark mark='e'/> and within a four-kilobyte page in two hundred and fifty-six. An object split across two lines costs two accesses, and a load whose address matches an earlier store's in its low twelve bits can be held up by the processor, which compares only those bits at first. Which case you get depends on the environment.
b8bc379c166f.zh: 一个没人读的变量，为什么会有影响？<bookmark mark='a'/>Linux 启动一个程序时，会把环境字符串和参数复制到新栈的最顶端，然后是指向它们的指针，只有在这些下面，程序自己的栈帧才开始。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以环境里每多一个字节，都会把每一个栈帧往下推。把一个热点局部变量的地址写成：栈顶，减去环境，再减去其他所有东西。<bookmark mark='c'/>调用约定让栈保持16字节对齐，所以这个地址以16字节为一步移动。<bookmark mark='d'/>在第9部分讲过的一个64字节的缓存行里，它可以落在4个位置上，<bookmark mark='e'/>而在一个4千字节的页里，可以落在256个位置上。一个跨越两个缓存行的对象，要访问两次；而一次读取，如果它的地址和前面某次存储的地址在低12位上相同，就可能被处理器拦住，因为处理器起初只比较这几位。你碰到哪种情况，取决于环境。

6c4faa01253b.en: Here is the first experiment from the hook again, with more of what we measured. <bookmark mark='a'/> For each of thirty-three environment sizes, from nothing to four kilobytes in steps of one hundred and twenty-eight bytes, we ran the program five times, interleaved, so that slow changes in the machine fall on every setting alike. The yellow dots are the medians; they spread by about seven percent. <bookmark mark='b'/> The blue dots are the fastest of each five; they spread by about five. <bookmark mark='c'/> Now, at the right, fifteen more runs of one unchanged setting, the empty environment, taken just after. They range over twenty-two percent, three times the whole spread of the medians. Before we blame the stack for anything, we have to know how much the machine moves on its own.
6c4faa01253b.zh: 这又是开场的第一个实验，这次多给出一些我们测到的东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>对33种环境大小中的每一种，从空的到4千字节，每步128字节，我们把程序运行五次，交错进行，让机器里缓慢的变化平均地落在每一种设置上。黄色的点是中位数；它们相差大约百分之七。<bookmark mark='b'/>蓝色的点是每五次里最快的一次；它们相差大约百分之五。<bookmark mark='c'/>现在看右边：紧接着，又对一个不变的设置，也就是空环境，运行了15次。它们的范围是百分之22，是全部中位数波动的三倍。在把任何事归咎于栈之前，我们得先知道机器自己会动多少。

1547d031fe8d.en: The second experiment changes nothing in the source, only the order in which the linker is handed the three object files. <bookmark mark='a'/> The linker lays the code out in that order, so every function lands at a new address. That changes how the hot loop lines up with the blocks in which the processor fetches instructions, and which branch-predictor entries its branches share. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here are fifteen runs of each order, with the environment empty. The medians differ by under one percent, far inside the scatter of the runs. <bookmark mark='c'/> On this machine, for this small loop, link order shows no effect we can detect. That is not the same as no effect: an effect smaller than the noise would look exactly like this.
1547d031fe8d.zh: 第二个实验不改源代码里的任何东西，只改交给链接器的三个目标文件的顺序。<bookmark mark='a'/>链接器按这个顺序排布代码，所以每个函数都落到一个新地址上。这会改变热循环与处理器取指令所用的块怎样对齐，也会改变它的分支共用分支预测器的哪些表项。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是每种顺序各运行15次的结果，环境为空。中位数相差不到百分之一，远远落在各次运行的散布之内。<bookmark mark='c'/>在这台机器上，对这个小循环，链接顺序没有显示出我们能检测到的效应。这和没有效应不是一回事：一个比噪声还小的效应，看起来恰恰就是这样。

2a18c5ee5132.en: This is what Todd Mytkowicz, Amer Diwan, Matthias Hauswirth and Peter Sweeney reported at ASPLOS in 2009, under the title Producing Wrong Data Without Doing Anything Obviously Wrong. <bookmark mark='a'/> They found measurement bias on every processor and both compilers they tried, and in most of the SPEC CPU2006 C programs. Changing the environment size or the link order could change whether the compiler's O3 setting looked faster than O2. Of more than a hundred recent papers they surveyed, none had adequately accounted for it. <bookmark mark='b'/> They proposed two remedies. Setup randomization: measure under many randomly chosen setups, and report the distribution, not one lucky point. <bookmark mark='c'/> And causal analysis: when you believe an effect has a cause, change that cause alone, and check that the effect follows. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 2013 Charlie Curtsinger and Emery Berger built Stabilizer, which keeps re-randomizing the layout while the program runs.
2a18c5ee5132.zh: 这正是 Todd Mytkowicz、Amer Diwan、Matthias Hauswirth 和 Peter Sweeney 2009年在 ASPLOS 上报告的，论文标题是《没做任何明显的错事，却产生了错误的数据》（Producing Wrong Data Without Doing Anything Obviously Wrong）。<bookmark mark='a'/>他们在试过的每一种处理器和两种编译器上，以及大多数 SPEC CPU2006 的 C 程序里，都发现了测量偏差。改变环境大小或链接顺序，就可能改变编译器的 O3 设置看起来是否比 O2 更快。在他们调查的一百多篇近期论文中，没有一篇充分考虑到了这一点。<bookmark mark='b'/>他们提出了两种补救办法。设置随机化：在许多随机选择的设置下测量，报告分布，而不是一个碰巧的点。<bookmark mark='c'/>以及因果分析：当你认为一个效应有某个原因时，只改变那个原因，并检查效应是否随之而来。<bookmark mark='d'/>2013年，Charlie Curtsinger 和 Emery Berger 做出了 Stabilizer，它在程序运行时不断地重新随机化内存布局。

056e2331fb4e.en: So what does our measurement show? <bookmark mark='a'/> Suppose nothing but noise were acting. Draw thirty-three medians of five from the forty-five runs with an empty environment, measure their spread, and repeat that four thousand times. <bookmark mark='b'/> Noise alone typically gives about ten percent. Our seven percent sits well inside it. <bookmark mark='c'/> We have shown that the medians moved by seven percent while an unused variable grew, and by under one percent across link orders. <bookmark mark='d'/> We have not shown that the environment caused it. And there is a reason it may not have: on this machine, with address randomization on, Linux starts the stack at a different place on every run, in sixteen-byte steps. We checked: a tiny C program printed twenty different addresses in twenty runs. That is a setup randomization done for us, and it smears the alignment effect into every setting's noise. To find a cause, you would switch it off and intervene.
056e2331fb4e.zh: 那么，我们的测量说明了什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>假设起作用的只有噪声。从45次空环境的运行中，抽出33个中位数，每个取五次运行，测量它们的波动，再把这个过程重复4000次。<bookmark mark='b'/>单凭噪声，通常就会给出大约百分之十。我们的百分之七稳稳地落在其中。<bookmark mark='c'/>我们已经表明：当一个没用到的变量增大时，中位数变动了百分之七；在不同的链接顺序之间，变动不到百分之一。<bookmark mark='d'/>我们没有表明是环境造成了这个变动。而且，有一个理由让它可能根本没有起作用：在这台机器上，地址随机化是开着的，Linux 每次运行都让栈从不同的位置开始，以16字节为一步。我们核对过：一个很小的 C 程序在20次运行中打印出了20个不同的地址。这相当于替我们做了一次设置随机化，它把对齐效应抹进了每一种设置的噪声里。要找到原因，你得把它关掉，再去干预。

9d0fa605b584.en: We ran the Job in plain Python thirty times on the same text, about twenty-five million characters. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each dot is one run. Nothing changed between them, and still they spread out. <bookmark mark='b'/> Report the best run and you claim eight hundred and sixty-five milliseconds; report the worst and you claim nine hundred and sixty-two milliseconds, eleven percent slower; the mean is nine hundred and seven milliseconds. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 2007 Andy Georges, Dries Buytaert and Lieven Eeckhout surveyed how Java performance papers reported their timings, and found many gave a single number, the best of several runs or a mean, with no measure of how uncertain it was. <bookmark mark='d'/> They showed that such methods can mislead, even about which of two systems is faster, and argued for repeated runs and confidence intervals instead.
9d0fa605b584.zh: 我们用普通的 Python，在同一份文本上把那项任务运行了30次，文本大约有25百万个字符。<bookmark mark='a'/>每个点是一次运行。它们之间什么都没变，可它们还是散开了。<bookmark mark='b'/>报告最好的那次，你声称的是865毫秒；报告最差的那次，你声称的是962毫秒，慢了百分之11；平均值是907毫秒。<bookmark mark='c'/>2007年，Andy Georges、Dries Buytaert 和 Lieven Eeckhout 调查了 Java 性能论文怎样报告计时，发现许多论文只给出一个数，几次运行中最好的一次，或者一个平均值，却没有任何衡量它有多不确定的指标。<bookmark mark='d'/>他们表明，这样的方法可能会误导人，甚至会搞错两个系统哪一个更快；他们主张改用重复运行和置信区间。

ce7f7c54e4ae.en: Georges and his colleagues also separated two questions. <bookmark mark='a'/> A runtime with a just-in-time compiler, like Part 15's, starts slowly, interpreting, and speeds up as it compiles the hot code. Start-up performance is the time of the first iterations: to measure it, start the runtime many times and time the first iteration of each. <bookmark mark='b'/> Steady-state performance is the time after warm-up: within each run, iterate until the timings settle, average those, and still repeat across several fresh runs, because each run can compile the code a little differently. <bookmark mark='c'/> Our Job, in order. The Python we use has no just-in-time compiler, and the times show no trend: the slowest is run number eighteen. Warm-up is not the story here; the machine's own noise is.
ce7f7c54e4ae.zh: Georges 和同事们还区分了两个问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个带即时编译器的运行时，比如第15部分的那个，开始时很慢，在解释执行，随着它编译热点代码而变快。启动性能是最初几次迭代的时间：要测量它，就把运行时启动许多次，给每次的第一次迭代计时。<bookmark mark='b'/>稳态性能是预热之后的时间：在每次运行内部，反复迭代，直到计时稳定下来，对这些取平均，而且仍然要在几次全新的运行之间重复，因为每次运行编译代码的方式都可能略有不同。<bookmark mark='c'/>这是我们的那项任务，按运行顺序排列。我们用的 Python 没有即时编译器，计时也没有显示出任何趋势：最慢的是第18次运行。这里的关键不是预热，而是机器自己的噪声。

da95cbf0b72d.en: How sure is a mean? The textbook formula assumes the times follow a bell curve. The bootstrap, Bradley Efron's idea from 1979, assumes much less. <bookmark mark='a'/> Start with our thirty runs and their mean. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now treat the sample as if it were the whole world: draw thirty runs from it at random, with replacement, so that some appear twice and some not at all, and take the mean of that resample. <bookmark mark='c'/> Do it again, and again; each resample gives a slightly different mean. <bookmark mark='d'/> After thousands of resamples the means form a distribution, and its middle ninety-five percent is a ninety-five percent confidence interval: here from eight hundred and ninety-seven milliseconds to nine hundred and seventeen milliseconds. The same recipe works for a median, or for the ratio of two programs' times, where no textbook formula is at hand.
da95cbf0b72d.zh: 一个平均值有多可靠？教科书上的公式假定计时服从钟形曲线。自助法（bootstrap）是 Bradley Efron 1979年提出的想法，它的假定要少得多。<bookmark mark='a'/>从我们的30次运行和它们的平均值开始。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在把这个样本当作整个世界：从中有放回地随机抽取30次运行，这样有些会出现两次，有些一次也不出现，再取这个重抽样本的平均值。<bookmark mark='c'/>再做一次，再做一次；每个重抽样本给出的平均值都略有不同。<bookmark mark='d'/>经过几千次重抽样，这些平均值形成一个分布，它中间的95%，就是一个95%置信区间：这里是从897毫秒到917毫秒。同样的办法也适用于中位数，或者两个程序时间的比值，这些情形手头都没有现成的教科书公式。

fb8d8687c9f7.en: How many runs are enough? <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is the bootstrap interval after three, five, ten, twenty and thirty of our runs. It narrows: sixty-two milliseconds wide after three runs, twenty after thirty. <bookmark mark='b'/> Why that rate? Independent runs have variances that add, so the variance of a mean of n runs is the variance of one run divided by n. <bookmark mark='c'/> Take the square root: the spread of the mean falls as one over the square root of n. <bookmark mark='d'/> The interval is about four of those wide, so to halve it you need four times the runs. The dashed lines are that prediction, and our intervals follow it. <bookmark mark='e'/> Notice, too, that the centre drifts. The formula assumes the machine does not change while you measure; a shared machine does, which is why we interleave settings, and why an interval is only as honest as that assumption.
fb8d8687c9f7.zh: 要运行多少次才够？<bookmark mark='a'/>这是在我们运行了3、5、10、20和30次之后的自助法区间。它在变窄：三次运行之后，宽62毫秒；30次之后，宽20毫秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>为什么是这个速度？独立运行的方差可以相加，所以 n 次运行的平均值的方差，等于一次运行的方差除以 n。<bookmark mark='c'/>开平方：平均值的散布按 n 的平方根分之一下降。<bookmark mark='d'/>区间大约有四个这样的量那么宽，所以要把它减半，你需要四倍的运行次数。虚线就是这个预测，而我们的区间跟着它走。<bookmark mark='e'/>还要注意，中心在漂移。这个公式假定你测量的时候机器不变；而一台共享的机器会变，这就是我们为什么要把各种设置交错进行，也是为什么一个区间的诚实程度，只能和这个假定一样。

cc829a71ff97.en: Last, how to average speedups. <bookmark mark='a'/> Two programs on two benchmarks: A takes one second on the first and four on the second; B takes two on each. <bookmark mark='b'/> Divide B's times by A's and average: one and a quarter, so B is a quarter slower. Divide A's by B's instead and average: also one and a quarter, so A is a quarter slower. Both cannot be true. <bookmark mark='c'/> The geometric mean is the n-th root of the product of the ratios. <bookmark mark='d'/> Flip every ratio and it flips exactly, so it gives the same verdict whichever way round you divide, and whichever machine you normalize to. <bookmark mark='e'/> In logarithms it is an ordinary mean, where twice as fast and twice as slow cancel. Here it says one: a tie. Philip Fleming and John Wallace made this argument in 1986. <bookmark mark='f'/> But see what it does not say: run both benchmarks once each, and B finishes in four seconds, A in five. For a fixed workload, total time is the honest summary.
cc829a71ff97.zh: 最后，怎样对加速比取平均。<bookmark mark='a'/>两个程序，两个基准测试：A 在第一个上用1秒，在第二个上用4秒；B 在每个上都用2秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>用 B 的时间除以 A 的时间，再取平均：1.25，所以 B 慢了四分之一。反过来，用 A 的除以 B 的，再取平均：也是1.25，所以 A 慢了四分之一。两者不可能都对。<bookmark mark='c'/>几何平均数是这些比值之积的 n 次方根。<bookmark mark='d'/>把每个比值都倒过来，它也恰好倒过来，所以无论你按哪个方向相除，无论你以哪台机器为基准做归一化，它给出的结论都一样。<bookmark mark='e'/>取对数之后，它就是普通的平均值，快一倍和慢一倍在这里相互抵消。这里它给出的是1：打平。Philip Fleming 和 John Wallace 在1986年提出了这个论证。<bookmark mark='f'/>但要看清它没有说什么：把两个基准测试各跑一次，B 在4秒内跑完，A 要5秒。对一个固定的工作负载，总时间才是诚实的概括。

3a4fafb52850.zh: 第四章：基准测试与可复现性。

2f07b8a78b24.en: A benchmark is a promise: a program whose speed stands for the speed of the programs you care about. <bookmark mark='a'/> Reinhold Weicker's Dhrystone, from 1984, was small and synthetic. It fitted in a cache, and much of its time went into a few string operations that compilers and libraries could tune for it. <bookmark mark='b'/> The SPEC consortium, founded in 1988 by computer makers, chose real programs instead, and replaces its suite every few years. <bookmark mark='c'/> Yet its first suite included matrix300, a matrix multiplication. As Hennessy and Patterson recount, compilers learned to transform it so thoroughly that it measured that one trick, and it was dropped from the next suite. <bookmark mark='d'/> Later, libquantum, in the 2006 suite, became notorious for compiler speedups far beyond what other programs saw; it is not in the 2017 suite. Each time, a score rose while the programs people ran did not.
2f07b8a78b24.zh: 基准测试是一个承诺：一个程序，它的速度代表你所关心的那些程序的速度。<bookmark mark='a'/>Reinhold Weicker 1984年的 Dhrystone 很小，而且是人工合成的。它能整个放进缓存，它的大部分时间花在少数几个字符串操作上，编译器和库可以专门针对它来调优。<bookmark mark='b'/>由计算机制造商在1988年创立的 SPEC 联盟，改用真实的程序，并且每隔几年就更换一次它的测试套件。<bookmark mark='c'/>然而它的第一套测试里包含了 matrix300，一个矩阵乘法。正如 Hennessy 和 Patterson 所讲述的，编译器学会了把它变换得如此彻底，以至于它只测量了那一个技巧，于是它在下一套里被去掉了。<bookmark mark='d'/>后来，2006年套件里的 libquantum 声名狼藉，编译器给它带来的加速远远超过其他程序；2017年的套件里已经没有它了。每一次，分数上去了，而人们实际运行的程序却没有。

dfeca3c6051d.en: Economists have a name for this. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1975 Charles Goodhart observed that a statistical regularity tends to collapse once it is used as a lever of control; the anthropologist Marilyn Strathern later put it as: when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. <bookmark mark='b'/> A benchmark begins as a measure of what we want: fast real programs. Make the score a target, and effort flows into whatever raises it, including tuning for the benchmark itself. <bookmark mark='c'/> The score keeps rising, and the real programs stop following it. <bookmark mark='d'/> Sometimes it is deliberate. In 2013 several phones were found raising their clock speeds when they recognized a benchmark app, and in 2015 Volkswagen's diesel cars were found detecting the emissions test, and running cleaner only then.
dfeca3c6051d.zh: 经济学家给这种现象起了个名字。<bookmark mark='a'/>1975年，Charles Goodhart 观察到，一种统计规律一旦被用作控制的杠杆，往往就会失效；人类学家 Marilyn Strathern 后来把它表述为：当一个度量成为目标，它就不再是一个好的度量。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个基准测试开始时，是对我们想要的东西的度量：真实的程序跑得快。把分数变成目标，力气就会流向任何能抬高分数的东西，包括专门针对基准测试本身的调优。<bookmark mark='c'/>分数不断上升，而真实的程序不再跟着它走。<bookmark mark='d'/>有时这是故意的。2013年，人们发现有几款手机在识别出基准测试应用时会提高时钟频率；2015年，人们发现大众的柴油车能检测到排放测试，只在那时才排放得更干净。

bcceed51ab23.en: SPEC's answer to Goodhart is a careful score and strict rules. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each benchmark's time is divided into the time a fixed reference machine took, giving a ratio where bigger is better. <bookmark mark='b'/> The score is the geometric mean of the ratios, the mean from chapter three. <bookmark mark='c'/> Divide two machines' scores, and the reference times cancel, so the ranking does not depend on which reference machine was chosen. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then the rules. A base result must use one set of compiler flags for every benchmark in a language; a peak result may tune each. Every result discloses its hardware, software and flags, and is reviewed before SPEC publishes it. And when a benchmark breaks, it is retired with the next suite.
bcceed51ab23.zh: SPEC 对 Goodhart 的回答，是一种精心设计的分数和严格的规则。<bookmark mark='a'/>用一台固定的参考机器所用的时间，除以每个基准测试的时间，得到一个越大越好的比值。<bookmark mark='b'/>分数是这些比值的几何平均数，也就是第三章的那种平均。<bookmark mark='c'/>把两台机器的分数相除，参考时间就约掉了，所以排名不取决于选了哪台参考机器。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后是规则。基础（base）结果必须对同一种语言的每个基准测试使用同一组编译器选项；峰值（peak）结果可以逐个调优。每个结果都要公开它的硬件、软件和编译选项，并在 SPEC 发布之前经过审查。而当一个基准测试失效时，它会随下一套测试被淘汰。

acc8aea3880b.en: The same pressure acts on researchers. <bookmark mark='a'/> Between the runs and the claim lie many reasonable choices: the mean, the median or the fastest run; whether to trim outliers; which benchmarks to show. In 2011 Joseph Simmons, Leif Nelson and Uri Simonsohn showed, for psychology, that freely combining such choices can make almost anything look significant; Andrew Gelman and Eric Loken called it the garden of forking paths. <bookmark mark='b'/> An honest test at the five percent level raises a false alarm one time in twenty, and stays quiet nineteen times in twenty. <bookmark mark='c'/> Over k independent tries, the chance that all stay quiet is that, to the power k, <bookmark mark='d'/> so the chance of at least one is one minus it, <bookmark mark='e'/> and with twenty tries about sixty-four percent. <bookmark mark='f'/> In systems research, pick our fastest environment size against our slowest, and you have a seven percent speedup from a variable the program never reads. The remedies: decide the analysis before you see the results, report every benchmark and every run, and randomize the setup.
acc8aea3880b.zh: 同样的压力也作用在研究者身上。<bookmark mark='a'/>在运行和结论之间，有许多合理的选择：用平均值、中位数，还是最快的一次；要不要剔除离群值；展示哪些基准测试。2011年，Joseph Simmons、Leif Nelson 和 Uri Simonsohn 在心理学中表明，随意组合这些选择，几乎能让任何东西看起来都显著；Andrew Gelman 和 Eric Loken 把它叫作“小径分岔的花园”。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个在5%水平上的诚实检验，每20次会误报1次，另外19次保持安静。<bookmark mark='c'/>在 k 次独立尝试中，全部保持安静的概率是这个数的 k 次方，<bookmark mark='d'/>所以至少误报一次的概率是1减去它，<bookmark mark='e'/>尝试20次时，大约是百分之64。<bookmark mark='f'/>在系统研究中，拿我们最快的环境大小和最慢的相比，你就从一个程序从来不读的变量那里，得到了百分之七的加速。补救办法是：在看到结果之前就定好分析方法，报告每一个基准测试和每一次运行，并且把设置随机化。

f2252193bc13.en: The last defence is to let others check. <bookmark mark='a'/> The ACM distinguishes three levels. A result is repeatable when the same team gets it again with the same setup; reproducible when another team gets it using the authors' artifacts; and replicable when another team gets it with a setup of its own. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 2016 Christian Collberg and Todd Proebsting reported trying to obtain and build the code behind hundreds of systems papers; for many, they could not. <bookmark mark='c'/> Since 2011, many conferences have run artifact evaluation: a committee runs the authors' code and data, and papers earn badges for artifacts that are available, that work, and whose results were reproduced. <bookmark mark='d'/> This series keeps the same rule. Every measured number on screen is computed by code in the repository, cached, and recomputed by one command, so that anyone can check it.
f2252193bc13.zh: 最后一道防线，是让别人来检验。<bookmark mark='a'/>ACM 区分了三个层次。如果同一个团队用同样的设置再次得到某个结果，它就是可重复的（repeatable）；如果另一个团队用作者的制品（artifact）得到它，它就是可复现的（reproducible）；如果另一个团队用自己的一套设置得到它，它就是可复制的（replicable）。<bookmark mark='b'/>2016年，Christian Collberg 和 Todd Proebsting 报告说，他们尝试获取并构建数百篇系统论文背后的代码；其中许多，他们都做不到。<bookmark mark='c'/>从2011年起，许多会议开展了制品评估：一个委员会运行作者的代码和数据，论文可以因制品而获得徽章，分别表示制品可以获取、能够工作，以及结果已被复现。<bookmark mark='d'/>这个系列遵守同样的规则。屏幕上每一个测量出来的数，都由代码库里的代码计算出来，存进缓存，并能用一条命令重新计算，这样任何人都能检验它。

6f756a7ab510.zh: 第五章：作为研究的证明。

1192bf190f9a.en: A conjecture is a statement someone believes and nobody has proved. <bookmark mark='a'/> In letters in 1742, Christian Goldbach and Leonhard Euler arrived at this one: every even number above two is a sum of two primes. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then comes evidence: by 2014 it had been checked for every even number up to four times ten to the eighteenth, and it is still a conjecture. <bookmark mark='c'/> It can leave that state in only two ways. A counterexample refutes it, as a computer search refuted a conjecture of Euler's in 1966. <bookmark mark='d'/> Or a proof makes it a theorem, as for the four colours in 1976, in Part 18. <bookmark mark='e'/> And then the proof itself is checked: in 2005, by a proof assistant.
1192bf190f9a.zh: 猜想是有人相信、却还没有人证明的命题。<bookmark mark='a'/>1742年，Christian Goldbach 和莱昂哈德·欧拉在通信中得出了这样一个猜想：每个大于2的偶数都是两个素数之和。<bookmark mark='b'/>接着是证据：到2014年，它已经对直到4乘10的18次方的每个偶数核对过，而它仍然是一个猜想。<bookmark mark='c'/>它只能以两种方式离开这种状态。一个反例驳倒它，就像1966年一次计算机搜索驳倒了欧拉的一个猜想。<bookmark mark='d'/>或者一个证明让它成为定理，就像1976年的四色问题，见第18部分。<bookmark mark='e'/>然后，证明本身也要被检查：2005年，由一个证明助手完成。

75cea171eacb.en: What does a search prove? <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is our Goldbach check, simplified: sieve the primes, then for each prime in turn strike out the even numbers it completes. At the end, nothing is left. <bookmark mark='b'/> That run proves a theorem: every even number from four to two million is a sum of two primes. Finitely many cases, every one checked. <bookmark mark='c'/> Change one symbol, to any size at all, and it is Goldbach's conjecture, which no search can reach. <bookmark mark='d'/> What the search gives is a feel for the margin. The hardest case below two million, one million seventy-seven thousand four hundred and twenty-two, needs only six hundred and one, the one hundred and tenth prime; a counterexample would need every prime below half of n to fail.
75cea171eacb.zh: 一次搜索能证明什么？<bookmark mark='a'/>这是我们的 Goldbach 检查，简化过的：先用筛法筛出素数，然后依次对每个素数，划掉它能补成的那些偶数。到最后，什么都不剩。<bookmark mark='b'/>这次运行证明了一条定理：从4到200万的每个偶数，都是两个素数之和。有限多个情形，每一个都核对过。<bookmark mark='c'/>改动一个符号，改成任意大小，它就成了 Goldbach 猜想，而任何搜索都够不着它。<bookmark mark='d'/>搜索给你的，是对余量的感觉。200万以下最难的情形是1077422，它只需要601，也就是第110个素数；而一个反例，需要小于 n 的一半的每个素数都失败。

9071e4971d86.en: Our Collatz check is cleverer than it looks. <bookmark mark='a'/> Halve an even number, treble an odd one and add one. From seven the path climbs to fifty-two, then falls to five. <bookmark mark='b'/> There the program stops, because every start below seven already reaches one. <bookmark mark='c'/> That is strong induction, from Part 2: assume the claim for every smaller start; <bookmark mark='d'/> show that the path from n drops below n; <bookmark mark='e'/> then it holds for n. The computer proves that step for each n below one million, so every start below one million reaches one. <bookmark mark='f'/> Proving the step for every n is the whole Collatz problem.
9071e4971d86.zh: 我们的 Collatz 检查比看上去更巧妙。<bookmark mark='a'/>偶数减半，奇数乘3再加1。从7出发，路径爬升到52，然后落到5。<bookmark mark='b'/>程序在那里就停了，因为每个小于7的起点都已经到达1。<bookmark mark='c'/>这就是第2部分的强归纳法：假设对每个更小的起点结论都成立；<bookmark mark='d'/>证明从 n 出发的路径会降到 n 以下；<bookmark mark='e'/>那么结论对 n 也成立。计算机对每个小于1000000的 n 证明了这一步，所以每个小于1000000的起点都会到达1。<bookmark mark='f'/>对每一个 n 证明这一步，就是整个 Collatz 问题。

db5aff175fc6.en: Search shines when a conjecture is false. <bookmark mark='a'/> In 1769 Euler conjectured that it takes at least k k-th powers to add up to a k-th power: three cubes, four fourth powers, five fifth powers. <bookmark mark='b'/> So four fifth powers should never sum to a fifth power. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 1966 Leon Lander and Thomas Parkin searched by computer and found four that do. <bookmark mark='d'/> Check it: twenty-seven, eighty-four, one hundred and ten and one hundred and thirty-three, each to the fifth. <bookmark mark='e'/> The sum is exactly one hundred and forty-four to the fifth. Their note is a few lines long; it needed nothing else. <bookmark mark='f'/> Fourth powers fell in 1988: Noam Elkies found a counterexample, and Roger Frye's search found the smallest.
db5aff175fc6.zh: 搜索在猜想为假的时候最能大显身手。<bookmark mark='a'/>1769年，欧拉猜想，要至少 k 个 k 次方数才能加起来等于一个 k 次方数：三个立方数，四个四次方数，五个五次方数。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以四个五次方数之和永远不应该是一个五次方数。<bookmark mark='c'/>1966年，Leon Lander 和 Thomas Parkin 用计算机搜索，找到了这样的四个数。<bookmark mark='d'/>核对一下：27、84、110和133，各自的五次方。<bookmark mark='e'/>它们的和恰好是144的五次方。他们的短文只有几行长；它不需要别的东西。<bookmark mark='f'/>四次方的情形在1988年被攻破：Noam Elkies 找到了一个反例，而 Roger Frye 的搜索找到了最小的那个。

52737709f6d0.en: Sometimes the small cases lie. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give every number a sign: minus one if it has an odd number of prime factors, counted with repeats, plus one if even. Twelve is two times two times three: minus one. <bookmark mark='b'/> Primes get minus one; four, two times two, gets plus one. <bookmark mark='c'/> Keep a running total. It touches zero at two, four, six, ten and sixteen, and never rises above. <bookmark mark='d'/> George Pólya conjectured that it never does. <bookmark mark='e'/> In 1958 Brian Haselgrove proved it false without finding where, and in 1980 Minoru Tanaka found the first failure, near nine hundred and six million. A search to two million would have confirmed the conjecture more than four hundred times over.
52737709f6d0.zh: 有时候，小情形会撒谎。<bookmark mark='a'/>给每个数一个符号：如果它的素因数个数是奇数，重复的也算在内，就记负1；如果是偶数，就记正1。12是2乘2乘3：负1。<bookmark mark='b'/>素数得负1；4，也就是2乘2，得正1。<bookmark mark='c'/>维持一个累计和。它在2、4、6、10和16处碰到0，而从不升到0以上。<bookmark mark='d'/>George Pólya 猜想它永远不会升到0以上。<bookmark mark='e'/>1958年，Brian Haselgrove 证明了这个猜想是错的，却没有找到在哪里失败；1980年，Minoru Tanaka 找到了第一个失败点，在9亿600万附近。一次到200万的搜索，会让这个猜想看起来确定无疑，而第一个失败点，还远在这个范围的四百多倍之外。

7348f1e39eda.en: Each way of checking a proof asks you to trust something different. <bookmark mark='a'/> Part 2 proved that among six people, three are friends or three are strangers, in two lines, by pigeonholes. You trust the argument and its readers. <bookmark mark='b'/> Part 2 also checked all thirty-two thousand seven hundred and sixty-eight colourings by brute force. The four colour theorem, Thomas Hales's 1998 proof of Kepler's conjecture, and Part 26's two-hundred-terabyte proof work this way: you trust a program, its compiler and the machine. <bookmark mark='c'/> A proof assistant checks every inference, and you trust only its kernel, sixty-nine lines in Part 54. Four colours were checked this way in 2005, and Kepler by Hales's Flyspeck project in 2014. <bookmark mark='d'/> A theorem is only as sure as the least reliable thing you trust.
7348f1e39eda.zh: 每一种检查证明的方式，都要你信任不同的东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>第2部分用两行、靠鸽巢原理证明了：六个人里，要么有三个人彼此认识，要么有三个人彼此陌生。你信任的是论证和读它的人。<bookmark mark='b'/>第2部分还用穷举法检查了全部32768种着色。四色定理、Thomas Hales 1998年对开普勒猜想的证明，以及第26部分那个两百太字节的证明，都是这样做的：你信任的是一个程序、它的编译器和机器。<bookmark mark='c'/>证明助手检查每一步推理，你只需要信任它的内核，在第54部分里是69行。四色定理在2005年就是这样检查的，开普勒猜想则由 Hales 的 Flyspeck 项目在2014年检查完毕。<bookmark mark='d'/>一条定理的可靠程度，只等于你所信任的东西里最不可靠的那一个。

fad3a6a524bd.en: In 2007 Srinivasan Keshav published a short note called How to Read a Paper. Its advice is to read in three passes. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first takes five to ten minutes: the title, the abstract and the introduction; the section headings, but not what is under them; the conclusion; and a glance at the references. That is enough to decide whether to go on. <bookmark mark='b'/> The second pass takes up to an hour. Read everything except the proofs and the fine details, and read the figures with care: are the axes labelled, are there error bars, does each figure show what the text claims? Mark the references you have not read. <bookmark mark='c'/> The third pass is for a paper you must understand completely, or review. Keshav's instruction is to re-create the work: make the same assumptions as the authors, rebuild it, and compare. For a beginner, that can take many hours.
fad3a6a524bd.zh: 2007年，Srinivasan Keshav 发表了一篇短文，题为《如何阅读一篇论文》（How to Read a Paper）。它的建议是分三遍读。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一遍用五到十分钟：标题、摘要和引言；各节的标题，但不看下面的内容；结论；再扫一眼参考文献。这足以决定要不要继续读。<bookmark mark='b'/>第二遍最多用一个小时。除了证明和细枝末节，什么都读，而且要仔细读图：坐标轴标了吗？有误差线吗？每张图显示的，是正文所声称的东西吗？把你没读过的参考文献标出来。<bookmark mark='c'/>第三遍留给你必须完全理解、或者要评审的论文。Keshav 的指示是重新创造这项工作：做出和作者一样的假设，把它重建出来，再加以比较。对初学者来说，这可能要花许多个小时。

65a6924dca18.en: The first pass ends with five questions, which Keshav calls the five Cs. Here is an abstract to try them on. It is invented, for illustration. <bookmark mark='a'/> Category: what kind of paper is this? A systems paper: a new design, measured. <bookmark mark='b'/> Context: which other papers and which theory does it build on? Hash tables, from Part 17, and a related-work section we have not yet read. <bookmark mark='c'/> Correctness: do the assumptions appear to be valid? From an abstract, you cannot yet tell. <bookmark mark='d'/> Contributions: what does it add? One design and one speedup. <bookmark mark='e'/> Clarity: is it well written? Short, but vague in places. After five minutes you know whether to read on, and what to read for.
65a6924dca18.zh: 第一遍读完时，要回答五个问题，Keshav 称之为五个 C。这里有一篇摘要，可以拿来试一试。它是虚构的，只为说明问题。<bookmark mark='a'/>类别（Category）：这是哪一类论文？一篇系统论文：一种新设计，加上测量。<bookmark mark='b'/>背景（Context）：它建立在哪些别的论文和哪些理论之上？第17部分的哈希表，以及一节我们还没读的相关工作。<bookmark mark='c'/>正确性（Correctness）：这些假设看起来成立吗？光看摘要，你还说不准。<bookmark mark='d'/>贡献（Contributions）：它增加了什么？一种设计和一次加速。<bookmark mark='e'/>清晰度（Clarity）：它写得好吗？很简短，但有些地方含糊。五分钟之后，你就知道要不要读下去，以及读的时候要找什么。

f89b91c8fb4b.en: In the second pass, look for what is not said. Read the claim again, phrase by phrase, and ask what you would need in order to believe it. <bookmark mark='a'/> On thirty novels: which texts? Thirty novels are one sample of text, and chapter four showed how benchmarks fail. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two point one times faster: from how many runs, with what interval? Our own Job, run thirty times on the same text, spread by eleven percent. And if there were several inputs, how was the speedup averaged? <bookmark mark='c'/> Than the standard counter: which one, tuned by whom, on which machine? In chapter two, an unused environment variable moved our medians by six point seven percent. <bookmark mark='d'/> Little extra memory: how much is little? An adjective stands where a number belongs. <bookmark mark='e'/> And notice what is missing entirely: limitations, threats to validity, the code. When a paper names no weakness of its own, the reviewer has to find them.
f89b91c8fb4b.zh: 第二遍读的时候，要找那些没说出来的东西。把主张再读一遍，一个短语一个短语地读，问问自己需要什么才会相信它。<bookmark mark='a'/>“在三十部小说上”：哪些文本？三十部小说只是文本的一个样本，而第四章已经展示了基准测试是怎样失效的。<bookmark mark='b'/>“快2.1倍”：来自多少次运行，区间是多少？我们自己的那项任务，在同一份文本上运行30次，波动了百分之11。而如果有好几个输入，加速比是怎样取平均的？<bookmark mark='c'/>“比标准计数器”：哪一个，由谁调优，在哪台机器上？在第二章里，一个没用到的环境变量让我们的中位数变动了百分之6.7。<bookmark mark='d'/>“额外内存很少”：少是多少？一个形容词站在了本该是数字的位置上。<bookmark mark='e'/>还要注意完全缺失的东西：局限、效度威胁、代码。当一篇论文没有说出自己的任何弱点时，审稿人就得自己去找。

9094176194ee.en: The third pass is the hardest, and the one that teaches most. <bookmark mark='a'/> This part made one in chapter two, on the 2009 paper by Todd Mytkowicz, Amer Diwan, Matthias Hauswirth and Peter Sweeney: that link order and the size of the environment bias measurements. <bookmark mark='b'/> Rebuilding forces every unstated choice into the open. Which program? Which machine, and how busy? How many sizes, and how many runs? <bookmark mark='c'/> We had to answer each one ourselves, and we found an answer: thirty-three sizes, five runs each, a spread of six point seven percent, within the noise. <bookmark mark='d'/> And one question the reading alone would never have raised: does the stack start at the same address on every run? On this machine it does not. <bookmark mark='e'/> So the rebuild did not refute the paper. It found the paper's own remedy, setup randomization, already switched on.
9094176194ee.zh: 第三遍最难，也最能教会你东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>这一部分在第二章做过一次，对象是 Todd Mytkowicz、Amer Diwan、Matthias Hauswirth 和 Peter Sweeney 2009年的论文：链接顺序和环境的大小会让测量产生偏差。<bookmark mark='b'/>重建会逼着每一个没说出口的选择暴露出来。哪个程序？哪台机器，有多忙？多少种大小，多少次运行？<bookmark mark='c'/>每一个问题我们都得自己回答，而我们找到了一个答案：33种大小，每种运行五次，波动百分之6.7，在噪声之内。<bookmark mark='d'/>还有一个光靠阅读永远不会提出的问题：栈每次运行都从同一个地址开始吗？在这台机器上不是。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以，这次重建并没有驳倒那篇论文。它发现，论文自己提出的补救办法，设置随机化，早就开着了。

0fadb4d433d0.en: Reviewing is reading with a duty attached. Most review forms ask for the same few things. <bookmark mark='a'/> First a summary, in your own words, so that the authors can see you understood them. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then the strengths: say what is good, and mean it. <bookmark mark='c'/> Then the weaknesses, and here the craft is to separate what is fatal from what can be fixed, and for each fixable flaw, to say what would fix it. Judge the paper that was submitted, not the one you would have written. <bookmark mark='d'/> Then questions the authors can answer. <bookmark mark='e'/> And a verdict, with your confidence in it. A review is confidential, and it is written to a person: specific, courteous and checkable. Alan Jay Smith's guide for referees, The Task of the Referee, from 1990, is still worth reading.
0fadb4d433d0.zh: 评审，是带着责任的阅读。大多数评审表要的都是同样几样东西。<bookmark mark='a'/>首先是一份概述，用你自己的话写，让作者能看出你理解了他们。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后是优点：说出哪里好，而且要真心实意。<bookmark mark='c'/>然后是缺点，这里的功夫在于把致命的和可以修补的分开，而对每一个可修补的缺陷，要说出怎样修补。评判的是投来的这篇论文，而不是你自己会写的那篇。<bookmark mark='d'/>然后是作者能回答的问题。<bookmark mark='e'/>还有一个评定，以及你对它有多大把握。评审是保密的，而且是写给一个人看的：具体、礼貌、可检验。Alan Jay Smith 1990年给审稿人写的指南《审稿人的任务》（The Task of the Referee），至今仍然值得一读。

e3d160d6c316.en: In 1986 Richard Hamming, who spent three decades at Bell Labs, gave a talk called You and Your Research. Its best-known story is about lunch. <bookmark mark='a'/> Hamming sat with the chemists and asked what the important problems of their field were. A week later he asked which important problems they were working on. And later still: if what you are doing is not important, why are you working on it? <bookmark mark='b'/> He was careful about what important means. <bookmark mark='c'/> Time travel, teleportation and antigravity would matter enormously, he said, but they are not important problems, because we have no attack. <bookmark mark='d'/> A problem is important when it would matter and you can see a way in. <bookmark mark='e'/> Great scientists, he observed, keep ten to twenty such problems in mind, and when a new idea bears on one, they drop other things and go after it.
e3d160d6c316.zh: 1986年，在贝尔实验室工作了三十年的 Richard Hamming 做了一次演讲，题为《你和你的研究》（You and Your Research）。其中最有名的故事是关于午饭的。<bookmark mark='a'/>Hamming 和化学家们坐在一起，问他们这个领域的重要问题是什么。一个星期后，他问他们正在研究哪些重要问题。再后来又问：如果你做的事情不重要，你为什么要做它？<bookmark mark='b'/>他对“重要”的含义很讲究。<bookmark mark='c'/>他说，时间旅行、瞬间传送和反重力，意义会极其重大，但它们不是重要问题，因为我们没有下手的办法。<bookmark mark='d'/>一个问题之所以重要，是因为它意义重大，而你又能看到一条进去的路。<bookmark mark='e'/>他观察到，伟大的科学家脑子里总装着十到二十个这样的问题，一旦有个新想法和其中某一个有关，他们就放下别的事情，去追它。

75cd87ff252f.en: Hamming said that knowledge and productivity are like compound interest: of two people of about the same ability, one who works ten percent more will, over a career, produce more than twice as much. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the metaphor literally, as an illustration: grow ten percent a year on top of what you already have, and after n years the ratio is one point one to the n. <bookmark mark='b'/> When is that two? <bookmark mark='c'/> Take logarithms: n times the log of one point one equals the log of two. <bookmark mark='d'/> So n is about nought point six nine three over nought point nought nine five: just over seven years. <bookmark mark='e'/> The talk has other habits too: keep your door open, for the clues that interruptions bring, and keep Friday afternoons for great thoughts.
75cd87ff252f.zh: Hamming 说，知识和产出就像复利：两个能力差不多的人，一个多努力百分之十，一辈子下来，产出会是另一个的两倍多。<bookmark mark='a'/>把这个比喻当真，当作一个示意：在已有的基础上每年增长百分之十，n 年之后，比值就是1.1的 n 次方。<bookmark mark='b'/>它什么时候等于2？<bookmark mark='c'/>取对数：n 乘以1.1的对数，等于2的对数。<bookmark mark='d'/>所以 n 大约是0.693除以0.095：七年多一点。<bookmark mark='e'/>这次演讲还讲了别的习惯：把门开着，好接住打扰带来的线索；把星期五下午留给伟大的思考。

a5bb9dd827e4.en: George Pólya's How to Solve It, from 1945, is a short book about finding solutions. <bookmark mark='a'/> It has four phases: understand the problem, devise a plan, carry it out, and look back. <bookmark mark='b'/> For the plan, it offers questions. Do you know a related problem? A special case, or a more general one? Can you draw a figure, or work backwards? <bookmark mark='c'/> Pólya's own example: bring up exactly six quarts of water with a four-quart pail and a nine-quart pail. Start from the goal. <bookmark mark='d'/> Six in the big pail is nine less three. <bookmark mark='e'/> The small pail takes exactly three if it already holds one. <bookmark mark='f'/> And one is nine less four, less four again. <bookmark mark='g'/> Read the chain forwards: that is the solution. Part 2 searched every state of a jug puzzle; working backwards needs no search.
a5bb9dd827e4.zh: George Pólya 1945年的《怎样解题》（How to Solve It）是一本讲怎样找到解法的小书。<bookmark mark='a'/>它分四个阶段：理解问题，拟定计划，执行计划，以及回顾。<bookmark mark='b'/>为了拟定计划，它给出了一些问题。你知道一个相关的问题吗？一个特殊情形，或者一个更一般的情形？你能画个图吗，或者倒着推？<bookmark mark='c'/>Pólya 自己的例子：用一个4夸脱的桶和一个9夸脱的桶，恰好打上来6夸脱的水。从目标出发。<bookmark mark='d'/>大桶里的6，是9减3。<bookmark mark='e'/>小桶如果已经装着1，就恰好能再装进3。<bookmark mark='f'/>而1是9减4，再减4。<bookmark mark='g'/>把这条链正着读：那就是解法。第2部分搜索了一个水壶问题的每一个状态；倒着推则不需要搜索。

b03eb656d4be.en: A limit study measures the headroom before you spend years chasing it. <bookmark mark='a'/> Part 7 asked how good branch prediction could be on the Job. Two-bit counters mispredict eight point eight branches in a hundred; our TAGE, at nine kilobytes, five point seven. <bookmark mark='b'/> With no storage limit at all, two point five. So storage alone can win about three more in a hundred, and the rest needs a different kind of predictor. <bookmark mark='c'/> Amdahl's law is a limit study in one line: make a fraction p of the work s times faster. <bookmark mark='d'/> Let s grow without bound, and the gain is capped at one over one minus p. <bookmark mark='e'/> The Job spent ninety-nine point seven percent of its instructions in one linear search, so removing it could give at most three hundred and fifty times. <bookmark mark='f'/> The ledger shows the headroom was real: fifty-eight seconds in Part 13, under a second with Part 17's hash table.
b03eb656d4be.zh: 极限研究在你花上好几年去追逐提升空间之前，先把它测出来。<bookmark mark='a'/>第7部分问过：在那项任务上，分支预测最好能有多好。两位计数器每一百个分支预测错8.8个；我们9千字节的 TAGE，错5.7个。<bookmark mark='b'/>完全没有存储限制时，错2.5个。所以单靠存储，每一百个大约能再多赢回三个，剩下的需要另一类预测器。<bookmark mark='c'/>阿姆达尔定律就是一行字的极限研究：把工作中比例为 p 的部分加速 s 倍。<bookmark mark='d'/>让 s 无限增大，收益的上限就是1除以（1减 p）。<bookmark mark='e'/>那项任务有百分之99.7的指令花在一次线性查找上，所以去掉它，最多能快350倍。<bookmark mark='f'/>账本表明这个提升空间是真实存在的：第13部分要58秒，用上第17部分的哈希表后，不到1秒。

6ea4fff396ec.en: Working backwards scales up to research: start from the ideal, and ask what stands in the way. <bookmark mark='a'/> For a cache the ideal is known. In 1966 Laszlo Belady described it: evict the block that will be needed furthest in the future, and no policy misses less. <bookmark mark='b'/> What stands in the way is that the future is unknown. <bookmark mark='c'/> So the problem is to predict reuse from the past, and every policy, from least recently used onwards, can be measured by how close it comes. <bookmark mark='d'/> The Job too: the ideal is to touch each byte once, and Part 60 built that in hardware, about thirty-one milliseconds. Part 17's hash table spends about twenty-nine cycles on each byte, so the problem is less work per byte. <bookmark mark='e'/> The ideal says what success would be worth, the obstacle names the problem, and Hamming's test asks whether you have an attack.
6ea4fff396ec.zh: 倒着推可以放大到研究上：从理想出发，问问是什么挡在路上。<bookmark mark='a'/>对缓存来说，理想是已知的。1966年，Laszlo Belady 描述了它：逐出在未来最晚才会被用到的那个块，没有任何策略的缺失比它更少。<bookmark mark='b'/>挡在路上的是：未来是未知的。<bookmark mark='c'/>所以问题就是从过去预测复用，而每一种策略，从最近最少使用开始，都可以用它离理想有多近来衡量。<bookmark mark='d'/>那项任务也是如此：理想是每个字节只碰一次，而第60部分用硬件做到了这一点，大约31毫秒。第17部分的哈希表在每个字节上大约花29个周期，所以问题就是减少每个字节的工作量。<bookmark mark='e'/>理想告诉你成功值多少，障碍点出问题是什么，而 Hamming 的检验问的是：你有没有下手的办法。

b82127fad03c.en: Writing up research is making an argument, and in 1958 the philosopher Stephen Toulmin drew the shape of one. Take this part's own result from chapter two. <bookmark mark='a'/> The claim is what you want the reader to accept: an unused environment variable did not measurably change the program's speed. <bookmark mark='b'/> The data are the facts it rests on: the medians spread by six point seven percent across thirty-three sizes, five runs each. <bookmark mark='c'/> The warrant is why those data support the claim: noise alone, with no variable at all, gives spreads this large. <bookmark mark='d'/> The backing is why the warrant holds: four thousand simulated experiments. <bookmark mark='e'/> The qualifier says how far the claim reaches: on this machine, for this program. <bookmark mark='f'/> And the rebuttal says when it would fail: unless address randomization is hiding a real effect. Weak papers stop at the claim and the data.
b82127fad03c.zh: 把研究写出来，就是在构造一个论证；1958年，哲学家 Stephen Toulmin 画出了论证的形状。拿这一部分第二章自己的结果来说。<bookmark mark='a'/>主张（claim）是你想让读者接受的东西：一个没用到的环境变量，没有可测量地改变程序的速度。<bookmark mark='b'/>数据（data）是它所依据的事实：在33种大小上，每种运行五次，中位数相差百分之6.7。<bookmark mark='c'/>依据（warrant）说明这些数据为什么支持这个主张：单凭噪声，根本没有那个变量，也会给出这么大的波动。<bookmark mark='d'/>支撑（backing）说明依据为什么成立：4000次模拟实验。<bookmark mark='e'/>限定（qualifier）说明主张能延伸多远：在这台机器上，对这个程序。<bookmark mark='f'/>而反驳（rebuttal）说明它什么时候会失效：除非地址随机化正掩盖着一个真实的效应。薄弱的论文止步于主张和数据。

f2451c9ae990.en: A paper makes many claims, and each one needs its own evidence. Here is a test you can run on any draft, shown on chapter six's invented paper. <bookmark mark='a'/> First, list every claim the introduction makes, including the ones in passing. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then find, for each claim, the section, figure or theorem that supports it. Skim hashes each word once: that is the algorithm, in section three. Two point one times faster: figure four, if it has intervals and names its baseline. <bookmark mark='c'/> Little extra memory, and works for any language: nothing in the paper supports either. <bookmark mark='d'/> Each such claim must be cut, or the evidence added. A reviewer will run this test whether you do or not. A good introduction makes it easy, by saying where each contribution is shown.
f2451c9ae990.zh: 一篇论文会提出许多主张，每一个都需要它自己的证据。这里有一个可以在任何草稿上做的检验，用第六章那篇虚构的论文来演示。<bookmark mark='a'/>首先，列出引言提出的每一个主张，包括顺带提到的那些。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后，为每个主张找到支持它的那一节、那张图或那条定理。“Skim 对每个词只做一次哈希”：这是算法，在第3节。“快2.1倍”：图4，前提是它有区间，并且说明了基线是什么。<bookmark mark='c'/>“额外内存很少”，以及“适用于任何语言”：论文里没有任何东西支持这两条。<bookmark mark='d'/>每一条这样的主张，要么删掉，要么补上证据。无论你做不做，审稿人都会做这个检验。一篇好的引言会让它变得容易：说清楚每一项贡献在哪里得到展示。

7a8a59c5af87.en: A figure should carry the claim, and the same data can be made to carry opposite ones. These are chapter two's three link orders. <bookmark mark='a'/> On the left, only the medians, with the axis cut just below the smallest. The tallest bar stands seven point six times taller than the shortest, and the title announces that link order changes speed. <bookmark mark='b'/> On the right, the same experiment: every one of the forty-five runs, the medians marked, and an axis that shows the spread. The medians differ by under one percent; the runs within each order spread by eighteen to thirty-five percent. <bookmark mark='c'/> And its title states the claim the figure supports. Edward Tufte, in 1983, put the rule this way: the representation of numbers should be directly proportional to the quantities they represent. Show the spread, label the units, and let the reader check you.
7a8a59c5af87.zh: 一张图应该承载主张，而同样的数据，可以被做得承载相反的主张。这是第二章的三种链接顺序。<bookmark mark='a'/>左边只有中位数，坐标轴在最小值下方一点点就截断了。最高的柱子是最矮那根的7.6倍高，而标题宣称链接顺序会改变速度。<bookmark mark='b'/>右边是同一个实验：全部45次运行，标出了中位数，坐标轴能显示出波动。中位数相差不到百分之一；每种顺序内部的各次运行，波动在百分之18到百分之35之间。<bookmark mark='c'/>它的标题陈述的，是这张图所支持的主张。Edward Tufte 在1983年这样表述这条规则：数字的表示，应当与它们所代表的量成正比。展示波动，标明单位，让读者能检验你。

5eaf58260a6f.en: This series holds itself to a rule: every number on screen is computed by our own code, or is published and named. Here is how a computed number travels. <bookmark mark='a'/> An instrument, a Python module with its own tests, does the work: here, the measurement-bias experiment. <bookmark mark='b'/> A compute script runs each item once and stores the result in a cache, as JSON, under the part's name. <bookmark mark='c'/> A scene loads it. A scene never computes the experiment and never types a number in. <bookmark mark='d'/> And the narration is formatted from the same value, so the sentence you hear cannot disagree with the measurement. <bookmark mark='e'/> Rerun the instrument on another machine, and every chart and every sentence that depends on it changes with it. You need not trust us; you can check.
5eaf58260a6f.zh: 这个系列给自己定了一条规则：屏幕上的每一个数，要么由我们自己的代码算出来，要么已经发表并注明了出处。下面是一个计算出来的数怎样传递的。<bookmark mark='a'/>一个仪器，也就是一个带有自己测试的 Python 模块，负责做实际的工作：这里是测量偏差实验。<bookmark mark='b'/>一个计算脚本把每一项运行一次，把结果以 JSON 格式存进缓存，放在这一部分的名字下面。<bookmark mark='c'/>场景加载它。场景从不计算实验，也从不手敲一个数字。<bookmark mark='d'/>而旁白是用同一个值格式化出来的，所以你听到的句子不可能和测量结果不一致。<bookmark mark='e'/>在另一台机器上重新运行这个仪器，依赖它的每一张图、每一句话都会随之改变。你不必信任我们；你可以检验。

a3e4c2c02308.en: Three kinds of number appear in this series, and each wears its label. <bookmark mark='a'/> Computed numbers come from our instruments, on this machine, and say so: the six point seven percent spread, the hardest Goldbach case below two million, the limit of three hundred and fifty. <bookmark mark='b'/> Published numbers are named, with their authors and year, in the narration: Goldbach checked to four times ten to the eighteenth, Pólya's conjecture failing near nine hundred and six million. <bookmark mark='c'/> Illustrative numbers are marked on screen: the invented paper's two point one, chapter three's one second and four. <bookmark mark='d'/> Readers trust a writer who shows them how to check. Hamming put it bluntly: doing the work is not enough; you must write clearly and give talks, so that people will read and listen. Justin Zobel's Writing for Computer Science is the handbook for the first.
a3e4c2c02308.zh: 这个系列里出现三种数，每一种都带着自己的标签。<bookmark mark='a'/>计算出来的数来自我们的仪器，在这台机器上得出，并且会说明这一点：百分之6.7的波动，200万以下最难的 Goldbach 情形，350这个上限。<bookmark mark='b'/>已发表的数，会在旁白里注明作者和年份：Goldbach 猜想核对到4乘10的18次方，Pólya 猜想在9亿600万附近失效。<bookmark mark='c'/>示意性的数在屏幕上有标记：虚构论文里的2.1，第三章里的1秒和4秒。<bookmark mark='d'/>读者信任那些教他们怎样检验的作者。Hamming 说得很直白：把工作做出来是不够的；你必须写得清楚，还要去做报告，让人们会去读、会去听。Justin Zobel 的《计算机科学写作》（Writing for Computer Science）就是前一件事的手册。

bde991648d9f.en: Chapter nine, the frontier. What is still unknown, and where would you start?
bde991648d9f.zh: 第九章：前沿。还有什么是未知的？你又会从哪里开始？

221c64c9aa05.en: Here is every open problem the series met, as a sky over the tower. <bookmark mark='a'/> Each star is a question nobody has answered, labelled with the parts where we met it and the year it was first asked. Some are decades old: P against NP since 1971, the exponent of matrix multiplication since Strassen's surprise in 1969, the gate counts of circuits since Shannon in 1949. <bookmark mark='b'/> Some have moved recently: the fifth Busy Beaver number was proved in 2024, and the record for matrix multiplication keeps creeping down. <bookmark mark='c'/> None of them is closed, and each is someone's life's work. The rest of this chapter asks how a person would start on one.
221c64c9aa05.zh: 这是这个系列遇到过的每一个开放问题，画成塔上方的一片星空。<bookmark mark='a'/>每颗星都是一个没人回答过的问题，标着我们在哪些部分遇到它，以及它最早被提出的年份。有些已经有几十年了：P 与 NP，从1971年起；矩阵乘法的指数，从1969年施特拉森带来的惊喜起；电路的门数，从1949年的香农起。<bookmark mark='b'/>有些最近有了进展：第五个忙碌海狸数在2024年被证明，而矩阵乘法的纪录还在一点点往下降。<bookmark mark='c'/>它们没有一个已经解决，每一个都是某个人一生的工作。这一章剩下的部分要问：一个人会怎样着手其中的一个。

bda2faa98744.en: One honest way to start is with the small cases. <bookmark mark='a'/> In letters of 1742, Goldbach and Euler arrived at the conjecture that every even number above two is a sum of two primes. Our sieve checks every even number up to 2,000,000 in under a second, and finds that the hardest is 1,077,422, whose smallest prime partner is the largest. <bookmark mark='b'/> The Collatz problem, from 1937, says that halving even numbers and tripling-plus-one the odd ones always reaches one. Every start below a million does; the slowest takes 524 steps. <bookmark mark='c'/> Checking small cases never proves a theorem about all numbers, but it finds counterexamples, suggests patterns, and shows where a proof will have to work hardest.
bda2faa98744.zh: 一种诚实的起步方式，是从小情形入手。<bookmark mark='a'/>1742年，Goldbach 和欧拉在通信中得出了这个猜想：每个大于2的偶数都是两个素数之和。我们的筛法在不到1秒内，核对了直到2000000的每个偶数，并发现最难的是1077422，它最小的素数搭档是所有偶数里最大的。<bookmark mark='b'/>Collatz 问题出自1937年，它说：偶数减半，奇数乘3加1，最终总会到达1。每个小于一百万的起点都做到了；最慢的要走524步。<bookmark mark='c'/>核对小情形，永远证明不了一条关于所有数的定理，但它能找到反例，提示规律，并显示出证明在哪里得下最大的功夫。

679ed7519d32.en: How do you choose? <bookmark mark='a'/> Richard Hamming asked his colleagues what the important problems in their field were, and then why they were not working on them. <bookmark mark='b'/> Every problem marked with a star in this series has a smaller version that someone could finish. <bookmark mark='c'/> Many breakthroughs bring a new tool to an old problem: topology to agreement, spectra to flows, SAT to proofs. <bookmark mark='d'/> And a limit study, like Part 7's, tells you whether there is headroom worth having. <bookmark mark='e'/> So this last research problem is yours to define: pick one star from the series, find its smallest open special case, and settle it.
679ed7519d32.zh: 怎样选择？<bookmark mark='a'/>Richard Hamming 问他的同事们，他们领域里的重要问题是什么，然后问他们为什么不去研究这些问题。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个系列里每一个标了星号的问题，都有一个更小的版本，某个人是可以把它做完的。<bookmark mark='c'/>许多突破都是把一件新工具带到一个老问题上：把拓扑带到一致问题上，把谱带到流上，把 SAT 带到证明上。<bookmark mark='d'/>而一项极限研究，就像第7部分的那样，会告诉你有没有值得争取的提升空间。<bookmark mark='e'/>所以最后这道研究题，由你自己来定义：从这个系列里挑一颗星，找到它最小的、尚未解决的特殊情形，并解决它。

312658fcec3c.en: Chapter ten. Where the series meet.
312658fcec3c.zh: 第十章：几个系列交汇的地方。

b8f88c810bb8.en: This series has two older siblings: AI, Built, thirty-one parts on how machines learn, and Analysis, Built, ten parts on the mathematics of limits, from the real numbers to the spectral theorem. <bookmark mark='a'/> They share more than a style. These are the thirty novels that AI, Built's first part chose, from Pride and Prejudice to Ulysses. <bookmark mark='b'/> AI, Built trains its models on them, and scores every model on a passage none of them was trained on. <bookmark mark='c'/> This series' Job counts their words: about twenty-five million bytes, about four point six million words, from Part 6's Pebble to Part 60's circuit. <bookmark mark='d'/> Analysis, Built reads no novels at all, but it proves the theorems that the other two keep leaning on.
b8f88c810bb8.zh: 这个系列有两个年长的兄弟：《人工智能，从零搭建》，31个部分，讲机器怎样学习；以及《分析学，从零搭建》，10个部分，讲极限的数学，从实数一直讲到谱定理。<bookmark mark='a'/>它们共享的不只是一种风格。这是《人工智能，从零搭建》第1部分选出的三十部小说，从《傲慢与偏见》到《尤利西斯》。<bookmark mark='b'/>《人工智能，从零搭建》用它们训练模型，并在一段没有任何模型训练过的文字上，给每个模型打分。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个系列的那项任务数它们的词：大约25兆字节，大约4.6百万个词，从第6部分的 Pebble 一直数到第60部分的电路。<bookmark mark='d'/>《分析学，从零搭建》一部小说也不读，但它证明了另外两个系列一直依靠的那些定理。

17bf28d79c7b.en: Draw the three series as towers, one floor for each part: AI, Built on the left, this series in the middle, Analysis, Built on the right. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first bridge is the one every model crosses. Part 23 set gradient descent against Newton's method; AI, Built's Part 11 trains every network with descendants of that step: momentum, Adam, and learning-rate schedules. <bookmark mark='b'/> Part 57 asked when learning is possible at all, with PAC bounds and the VC dimension; AI, Built's Part 8 asks the same question of real models, with Rademacher complexity and double descent. <bookmark mark='c'/> Part 60 built a systolic array and put it on the roofline; AI, Built's Part 17 puts GPUs on the same roofline, and tiles matrix products to climb it. <bookmark mark='d'/> And Shannon's paper of 1948 sits under both. Part 28 proved his channel theorem with typical sets; AI, Built's first part met the same typical sets on the way to cross-entropy, the loss every language model is trained on.
17bf28d79c7b.zh: 把三个系列画成三座塔，每一部分一层：左边是《人工智能，从零搭建》，中间是这个系列，右边是《分析学，从零搭建》。<bookmark mark='a'/>第一座桥是每个模型都要跨过的那座。第23部分让梯度下降和牛顿法同台较量；《人工智能，从零搭建》的第11部分，用这一步的后代来训练每一个网络：动量、Adam，以及学习率调度。<bookmark mark='b'/>第57部分问过，学习到底什么时候是可能的，用的是 PAC 界和 VC 维；《人工智能，从零搭建》的第8部分对真实的模型问同一个问题，用的是 Rademacher 复杂度和双下降。<bookmark mark='c'/>第60部分搭了一个脉动阵列，并把它放到屋顶线上；《人工智能，从零搭建》的第17部分把 GPU 放到同一道屋顶线上，并对矩阵乘积分块，好爬上去。<bookmark mark='d'/>而香农1948年的论文，垫在这两者下面。第28部分用典型集证明了他的信道定理；《人工智能，从零搭建》的第1部分，在通往交叉熵的路上遇到了同样的典型集，而交叉熵正是每个语言模型训练时所用的损失。

b14cd1ba2f3e.en: On the other side stands analysis. <bookmark mark='a'/> The lowest bridge is the oldest. Turing's paper of 1936 was called On Computable Numbers: a real number is computable if a machine can write out its digits. Analysis, Built's first part builds the real numbers and proves, with Cantor's diagonal, that they are uncountable. Machines can be listed, so almost every real number is one that no machine can write. <bookmark mark='b'/> Part 19's fast Fourier transform, from Cooley and Tukey in 1965, computes the Fourier transform of Analysis, Built's Part 9, taken on a finite cycle of points instead of the whole line. <bookmark mark='c'/> And Part 52's iterations, Newton's method above all, converge for the reasons Analysis, Built's Part 2 proves: Cauchy sequences, and Taylor's theorem with its remainder, which also says how fast.
b14cd1ba2f3e.zh: 另一边是分析学。<bookmark mark='a'/>最低的那座桥最古老。图灵1936年的论文题为《论可计算数》（On Computable Numbers）：如果一台机器能写出一个实数的各位数字，这个实数就是可计算的。《分析学，从零搭建》的第1部分构造了实数，并用康托尔的对角线论证证明它们是不可数的。机器可以一一列出，所以几乎每一个实数，都是没有机器能写出来的。<bookmark mark='b'/>第19部分的快速傅里叶变换，来自1965年的 Cooley 和 Tukey，它计算的是《分析学，从零搭建》第9部分的傅里叶变换，只不过取在有限个点组成的一个环上，而不是整条直线上。<bookmark mark='c'/>而第52部分的迭代，首先是牛顿法，之所以收敛，原因正是《分析学，从零搭建》第2部分所证明的：柯西序列，以及带余项的泰勒定理，余项还说明了收敛有多快。

858f7d27f391.en: Some ideas stand on all three towers at once. Take the step that trains every model. <bookmark mark='a'/> Taylor's theorem, from Analysis, Built's Part 2: f at x plus h is f at x, plus the slope times h, plus half the second derivative at some point in between, times h squared. <bookmark mark='b'/> Now take Part 23's step: h is minus eta times the slope. The middle term becomes minus eta times the slope squared. <bookmark mark='c'/> If the curvature is never more than L, the last term is at most L over two, times eta squared, times the slope squared, so f falls by at least eta times one minus L eta over two, times the slope squared. <bookmark mark='d'/> Choose eta equal to one over L, and every step lowers f by at least the slope squared over two L. <bookmark mark='e'/> That inequality is why a learning rate has a ceiling, an early lesson of AI, Built's Part 11: step further than two over L, and the guarantee is gone. In many dimensions the slope becomes the gradient, the derivative of Analysis, Built's Part 4.
858f7d27f391.zh: 有些想法同时立在三座塔上。拿训练每个模型的那一步来说。<bookmark mark='a'/>《分析学，从零搭建》第2部分的泰勒定理：f 在 x 加 h 处的值，等于 f 在 x 处的值，加上斜率乘 h，再加上中间某一点处二阶导数的一半，乘以 h 的平方。<bookmark mark='b'/>现在取第23部分的那一步：h 等于负 eta 乘以斜率。中间那一项变成负 eta 乘以斜率的平方。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果曲率从不超过 L，最后一项至多是 L 除以2，乘 eta 的平方，再乘斜率的平方，所以 f 至少下降 eta 乘以（1减 L eta 除以2），再乘斜率的平方。<bookmark mark='d'/>取 eta 等于1除以 L，每一步至少让 f 下降斜率的平方除以2L。<bookmark mark='e'/>这个不等式说明了学习率为什么有一个上限，这是《人工智能，从零搭建》第11部分早早讲过的一课：步子迈得比2除以 L 还远，这个保证就没有了。在多维情形下，斜率变成梯度，也就是《分析学，从零搭建》第4部分的导数。

9c4db278288d.en: Draw every crossing at once, and three buildings start to look like one. <bookmark mark='a'/> There are more than these seven. Part 18's PageRank is a Markov chain from AI, Built's Part 5; Part 20's random projections are the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma of its Part 3; Part 54's proof assistants are the Lean of its Part 25. <bookmark mark='b'/> And a good research problem often lives on a bridge: a tool that is routine on one side, and not yet tried on the other.
9c4db278288d.zh: 把所有的交汇一次画出来，三座建筑开始看起来像一座。<bookmark mark='a'/>交汇不止这七处。第18部分的 PageRank，是《人工智能，从零搭建》第5部分的一条马尔可夫链；第20部分的随机投影，是它第3部分的 Johnson–Lindenstrauss 引理；第54部分的证明助手，就是它第25部分的 Lean。<bookmark mark='b'/>而一道好的研究题，常常就住在一座桥上：一件在一边已经是常规的工具，在另一边却还没人试过。

dfca3ff28ada.en: Chapter eleven. The pebble, the last time.
dfca3ff28ada.zh: 第十一章：最后一次看石子。

4e7ccb301e0c.en: Part 1 began with a game for someone who knows nothing about numbers: two piles of pebbles, and one rule. <bookmark mark='a'/> If the piles differ, take from the bigger as many as the smaller has. Twenty-four and eighteen become six and eighteen, then six and twelve, then six and six, <bookmark mark='b'/> and six is their greatest common divisor. <bookmark mark='c'/> In 1928 Hilbert and Ackermann asked whether every mathematical question could be settled like that, by a mechanical procedure that moves symbols the way the player moves stones: the Entscheidungsproblem. <bookmark mark='d'/> In 1936 Turing answered no, and to prove it he first had to say exactly what a mechanical procedure is. His answer was a machine, and everything else in this series was built on it.
4e7ccb301e0c.zh: 第1部分从一个给完全不懂数字的人玩的游戏开始：两堆石子，一条规则。<bookmark mark='a'/>如果两堆不一样多，就从大的那堆里拿走和小的那堆一样多的石子。24和18变成六和18，然后是六和12，然后是六和六，<bookmark mark='b'/>而六就是它们的最大公约数。<bookmark mark='c'/>1928年，希尔伯特和阿克曼问：是否每一个数学问题都能像这样解决，用一种机械的程序，像玩家移动石子那样移动符号：这就是判定问题（Entscheidungsproblem）。<bookmark mark='d'/>1936年，图灵回答：不能。而为了证明这一点，他首先必须准确地说出机械的程序是什么。他的答案是一台机器，而这个系列里的其他一切，都建立在它之上。

e9afdae3e2fe.en: Then the series climbed, from the mathematics at the bottom. <bookmark mark='a'/> Part 3 built every gate from one kind, NAND, <bookmark mark='b'/> and by Part 6 those gates were Pebble, a thirty-two-bit computer that ran the Job. <bookmark mark='c'/> Pipelines, caches and four cores made it fast; <bookmark mark='d'/> a linker, a compiler, types and garbage collectors let us speak to it; <bookmark mark='e'/> algorithms told it what to do. <bookmark mark='f'/> PebbleOS shared it among programs and kept their data on a disk; <bookmark mark='g'/> our own TCP, Raft and MapReduce joined many Pebbles; <bookmark mark='h'/> and the web, services and the cloud put the whole thing in front of people. <bookmark mark='i'/> Beside the stack stand two columns: the limits, what no machine can compute or keep secret, and the practice, how people build such things together. <bookmark mark='j'/> And in Part 55 we asked whether any of it could be trusted, and watched a compiler lie about itself, and a second compiler catch it.
e9afdae3e2fe.zh: 然后，这个系列从底部的数学开始往上爬。<bookmark mark='a'/>第3部分只用一种门，与非门（NAND），搭出了所有的门，<bookmark mark='b'/>到第6部分，这些门已经成了 Pebble，一台32位的计算机，它运行了那项任务。<bookmark mark='c'/>流水线、缓存和四个核让它变快；<bookmark mark='d'/>链接器、编译器、类型和垃圾回收器让我们能和它说话；<bookmark mark='e'/>算法告诉它该做什么。<bookmark mark='f'/>PebbleOS 让许多程序分享它，并把它们的数据保存在磁盘上；<bookmark mark='g'/>我们自己的 TCP、Raft 和 MapReduce，把许多台 Pebble 连在一起；<bookmark mark='h'/>而 Web、服务和云，把这一整套东西放到了人们面前。<bookmark mark='i'/>在这一叠层的旁边立着两根柱子：一根是极限，也就是任何机器都算不出来的东西、守不住的秘密；一根是实践，也就是人们怎样一起建造这样的东西。<bookmark mark='j'/>而在第55部分，我们问过这一切是否值得信任，看着一个编译器对自己撒谎，又看着第二个编译器把它揭穿。

3ed6df09ae35.en: The Job kept score the whole way: count the words of the thirty novels, and list the twenty most common. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is every row of the ledger, twenty-two of them, on a scale where each step is a factor of ten. Part 6's single-cycle Pebble needed two hundred and eighty-one seconds. <bookmark mark='b'/> Part fifteen's lambda-calculus machine took two point four hours, and caches, compilers, hash tables, kernels, networks and clusters pushed the bar back and forth. <bookmark mark='c'/> The last row is Part 60's word-counting circuit: about thirty-one milliseconds, if the text arrives a byte every cycle. Most rows are computed by the machines the series built; a few were timed natively on this one.
3ed6df09ae35.zh: 那项任务一路都在记分：数出三十部小说里的词，列出最常见的二十个。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是账本的每一行，一共22行，画在每一格相差十倍的刻度上。第6部分的单周期 Pebble 需要281秒。<bookmark mark='b'/>第15部分的λ演算机器用了2.4小时，而缓存、编译器、哈希表、内核、网络和集群，把这根柱子推来推去。<bookmark mark='c'/>最后一行是第60部分的数词电路：大约31毫秒，前提是文本每个周期到达一个字节。大多数行，是由这个系列搭建的机器算出来的；少数几行，是在这台机器上原生计时的。

9d127e57d452.en: So how much faster did the series make the Job? <bookmark mark='a'/> Divide the first row by the last: two hundred and eighty-one seconds over about thirty-one milliseconds, <bookmark mark='b'/> a speedup of about eight thousand nine hundred and thirty-two times. <bookmark mark='c'/> That ratio is a product of twenty-one steps, one from each row to the next, and they did not all point the same way. <bookmark mark='d'/> Nine of them went slower, because each row changed what was measured as well as how fast it ran, adding a kernel, a network or a cluster. The largest step forward was one thousand six hundred and ninety-nine-fold, from Part fifteen to Part sixteen; the largest step back, one hundred and forty-nine-fold, from Part thirteen to Part fifteen. <bookmark mark='e'/> And the typical step, by chapter three's rule for averaging ratios, is the twenty-first root of the total: about one point five four times faster, row after row.
9d127e57d452.zh: 那么，这个系列让那项任务快了多少？<bookmark mark='a'/>用第一行除以最后一行：281秒，除以大约31毫秒，<bookmark mark='b'/>加速比大约是8932倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>这个比值是21步的乘积，每一步从一行到下一行，而它们并不都指向同一个方向。<bookmark mark='d'/>其中9步变慢了，因为每一行既改变了运行的快慢，也改变了测量的对象：加上了一个内核、一个网络或者一个集群。向前最大的一步是1699倍，从第15部分到第16部分；向后最大的一步是149倍，从第13部分到第15部分。<bookmark mark='e'/>而典型的一步，按第三章对比值取平均的规则，是总数的21次方根：每一行大约快1.54倍。

e38c541fc6d8.en: At the top of the tower the floors stop, and the sky of chapter nine begins: <bookmark mark='a'/> P against NP, one-way functions, the exponent of matrix multiplication, the sixth Busy Beaver, and the rest, each met somewhere on the way up. <bookmark mark='b'/> Hilbert hoped that one procedure could settle every such question. Turing's answer means that no machine ever will, so this sky will never be empty: there will always be a question for someone to start on.
e38c541fc6d8.zh: 到了塔顶，楼层到头了，第九章的星空从这里开始：<bookmark mark='a'/>P 与 NP，单向函数，矩阵乘法的指数，第六个忙碌海狸数，还有其余的问题，每一个都是我们在往上爬的路上某处遇到的。<bookmark mark='b'/>希尔伯特曾希望，一种程序就能解决所有这样的问题。图灵的回答意味着，永远不会有任何机器做到这一点，所以这片天空永远不会空：总会有一个问题，等着某个人去着手。

d15bc02ec136.en: Every floor of that tower, and every star above it, began the way Part 1 did: <bookmark mark='a'/> with a small stone, moved by a rule. The Romans called such a stone a calculus. <bookmark mark='b'/> It is still the smallest thing a computer is made of: a mark that is either there or not, moved one rule at a time.
d15bc02ec136.zh: 那座塔的每一层，以及它上方的每一颗星，都是像第1部分那样开始的：<bookmark mark='a'/>从一颗小石子开始，按一条规则移动。罗马人把这样的石子叫作 calculus。<bookmark mark='b'/>它仍然是计算机由之构成的最小的东西：一个标记，要么在，要么不在，一次按一条规则移动。

8b1f6fa7b434.en: The last act went past the degree, to the first year of research. <bookmark mark='a'/> Eigenvalues that know a graph's shape; theorems about when learning is possible; three meanings for every program; the limits of what distributed processes can compute; hardware built for a single job; and, in this part, the methods by which every result in the series was made.
8b1f6fa7b434.zh: 最后一幕越过了学位，走进研究的第一年。<bookmark mark='a'/>知道一个图的形状的特征值；关于学习何时可能的定理；每个程序的三种含义；分布式进程能计算什么的极限；为单一工作而造的硬件；以及在这一部分，这个系列里每一个结果得以做出的方法。

a672b160f54a.en: And that is the whole map: sixty-one parts. <bookmark mark='a'/> It began with two piles of pebbles and a rule, and it ends on questions nobody can yet answer. Every layer was built on the one below it, and every one of them was built here, from gates to a cluster, from a proof to a protocol.
a672b160f54a.zh: 这就是整张地图：61个部分。<bookmark mark='a'/>它从两堆石子和一条规则开始，结束在一些还没有人能回答的问题上。每一层都建在它下面那一层之上，而每一层都是在这里搭起来的，从门到集群，从一个证明到一个协议。

7ac15b270909.en: Six problems, the last of the series, with full solutions in the part's notes. Pause on any of them. The fifth is a build problem: repeat this part's own experiment with the stack held still, and decide, with a permutation test, whether the effect that noise hid is really there. The last, marked with a star, is the research problem of chapter nine, and it is the series' last word: pick one open problem, find its smallest open case, and settle it.
7ac15b270909.zh: 六道习题，也是这个系列的最后几道，完整的解答在这一部分的笔记里。随时可以在任何一道上暂停。第五道是一道动手题：在栈保持不动的情况下，重做这一部分自己的实验，并用置换检验来判断，被噪声掩盖的那个效应是否真的存在。最后一道标了星号，是第九章的那道研究题，也是这个系列的最后一句话：挑一个开放问题，找到它最小的、尚未解决的情形，并解决它。

dfc3418ec26a.en: If you want to keep going, here is a shelf. <bookmark mark='a'/> For the machine, Harris and Harris, Patterson and Hennessy, and Bryant and O'Hallaron. For languages, Abelson and Sussman, Appel, and Pierce. For algorithms, the book by Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest and Stein, and Kleinberg and Tardos. For theory, Sipser, Arora and Barak, and Motwani and Raghavan. For systems, the Arpaci-Dusseaus, Kurose and Ross, and Kleppmann. For software, Brooks and Ousterhout. And for research itself, Hamming's lecture and Pólya's How to Solve It.
dfc3418ec26a.zh: 如果你想继续走下去，这里有一个书架。<bookmark mark='a'/>关于机器：Harris 和 Harris，Patterson 和 Hennessy，以及 Bryant 和 O'Hallaron。关于语言：Abelson 和 Sussman，Appel，以及 Pierce。关于算法：Cormen、Leiserson、Rivest 和 Stein 合写的那本书，以及 Kleinberg 和 Tardos。关于理论：Sipser，Arora 和 Barak，以及 Motwani 和 Raghavan。关于系统：Arpaci-Dusseau 夫妇，Kurose 和 Ross，以及 Kleppmann。关于软件：Brooks 和 Ousterhout。而关于研究本身：Hamming 的演讲，以及 Pólya 的《怎样解题》。

410cadbb09b5.en: This is the end of Computer Science, Built. Thank you for watching all of it. The open problems are real, and some of them will be solved by people who started exactly where this series did, with a few pebbles and a rule. Take one, and start.
410cadbb09b5.zh: 《计算机科学，从零搭建》到这里就结束了。感谢你把它全部看完。这些开放问题是真实的，其中一些会被这样的人解决：他们恰恰从这个系列起步的地方出发，带着几颗石子和一条规则。挑一个，开始吧。
